entries.title: Micah 5:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Now gather thyself - Since this must be done, do it quickly. O daughter of troops - Nineveh or Babylon. He - Sennacherib, or Nebuchadnezzar. They - The proud, oppressive enemy. The judge - The king. Of Israel - Not the ten tribes, though they are actually called by this name, but the two tribes that adhered to David's family. A rod - This is a proverbial speech, expressing the most contemptuous usage.

entries.title: Micah 5:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Bethlehem - Bethlehem of Judah was called Ephratah, from the fruitfulness of the land where it stood: the word whence it is derived importing fruitfulness. Art thou little - If thou art the least in other respects in this thou art honoured above them all. Ruler - King and sovereign. In Israel - Amidst the Israel of God. Going forth - Whose generation, as he is the Son of God, equal with his father, is eternal.

entries.title: Micah 5:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: This man - The Messiah. The peace - Which is promised to the people of God; all their deliverances are not only for his sake, but effected by his power. Shall tread in our palaces - Which Sennacherib did in all the cities of Judah, except Jerusalem. We - Hezekiah, and with him the prophets and people, shall prevail with God to send deliverance. Seven shepherds - A certain number put for an uncertain.

entries.title: Micah 5:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: They - The seven shepherds, and eight principal men, those great instruments of God's revenge, and his church's deliverance. Waste the land - So did Merodach Baladan, king of Babylon. The land of Nimrod - The same with the land of Assyria. The entrance - The fortified frontiers. In this manner shall he, the Messiah, deliver the Jews, his people. The Assyrian - The type of all other enemies, to the people of God.

entries.title: Micah 5:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: As a dew - This remnant wherever they are, shall multiply as the dew that refreshes the grass, so where this remnant is, it shall be a blessing to those about them, that use them friendly. As the showers - God shall bless them by his immediate hand, as he alone, without the help of man, gives dew and showers. As this was fulfilled in the type, before the gospel was preached to all nations, so it hath been, now is, and ever shall be fulfilled in ages to come. God's remnant shall be a blessing to the places they live in.

entries.title: Micah 5:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: As a lion - For strength and courage, which the beasts of the forest dare not oppose, and cannot resist.

entries.title: Micah 5:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: I will cut off - Not in judgment, but in mercy, for there shall be no need of them, nor shall the church of God any more rely on them. Thy chariots - Chariots prepared for war.

entries.title: Micah 5:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The cities - Cut off the occasion of fortifying their cities, thou shalt need no other defence than what I am to thee.

entries.title: Micah 5:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: I will cut off - God will in mercy to his people take away these occasions of sin.

entries.title: Micah 5:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Graven images - This was verified among the Jews, who to this day hate images for divine uses, and learnt this in their captivity.

entries.title: Micah 5:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Thy groves - The groves which they abused by idolatrous worship.

entries.title: Micah 5:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Have not heard - In an unprecedented manner. Christ will give his Son either the hearts or necks of his enemies, and make them either his friends or his footstool.
